The challenges Medicare Advantage (MA) poses to rural hospitals are stark, as highlighted by Avera Health’s experience in Nebraska. MA plans reimburse rural facilities at just 90.6% of Traditional Medicare rates—already below cost—forcing unsustainable financial strain. Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs), designed for cost-based reimbursement, face MA rates at 95% of costs, undermining their viability. Administrative burdens like prior authorization delays exacerbate this: rural MA patients endure 9.6% longer hospital stays awaiting post-acute care approvals, driving up costs.

The AHA estimates MA’s payment disparities cost rural hospitals over $1 billion in 2023 alone. Solutions like the Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act (H.R. 3173/S. 1298) aim to streamline prior authorization, while proposals for cost-based MA reimbursement for CAHs (H.R. 5434) could restore financial protections.

Without reforms, MA’s growth risks further closures—429 rural hospitals are already at high financial risk. Dr. Basel’s insights underscore the urgency of aligning MA policies with rural realities to preserve access.
